text:
Skip the hotel breakfast once in Osaka. Go where the chefs shop instead. 🐟

Most visitors only know one market in Osaka. Here's the one we'd send a friend to on a weekday morning.

━━━━━━━━━━
🏮 KIZU WHOLESALE MARKET
━━━━━━━━━━

A private wholesale market with more than 300 years of history.

Restaurant chefs come here for fish, vegetables and dried goods, and visitors can walk in and buy too.

It's quieter and less polished than the famous markets. That's exactly the point.

━━━━━━━━━━
🚇 HOW TO GET THERE
━━━━━━━━━━

• Osaka Metro Midosuji or Yotsubashi Line to Daikokucho
• Take Exit 1
• About 3 minutes on foot

━━━━━━━━━━
⏰ WHEN TO GO
━━━━━━━━━━

• Best between 8:30 and 10:30
• Stalls open around dawn for chefs, and many close by late morning
• Closed Sundays and national holidays, some Wednesdays, and 31 Dec – 4 Jan
• The calendar is on kizu-ichiba.com, so check it the night before

━━━━━━━━━━
🍣 HOW WE'D DO IT
━━━━━━━━━━

Skip the hotel breakfast. Ride the subway to Daikokucho, eat a seafood bowl at the market, then walk back into the city with the whole day still ahead of you.

━━━━━━━━━━
➕ TWO MORE LOCAL MARKETS
━━━━━━━━━━

🥩 Tsuruhashi Market: a maze of covered lanes right outside Tsuruhashi Station, full of yakiniku restaurants, Korean grocers and fish stalls. Come hungry in the evening. Many small shops prefer cash.

🛍️ Tenjinbashisuji: a 2.6 km covered shopping street used by locals every day, about 40 minutes end to end. A good rainy-day walk.

Full guide with all three markets and the best time for each 👉 https://japanbystation.com/osaka-local-markets

Would you trade a hotel breakfast for this? 👇
